Heat uses comments, positive reactions and repository stars. Coverage order rotates domains and takes one issue per repository in each round. Search hits are never counted as CoroPerf successes.

Each repository keeps its discussion head and recent-update windows. When more results exist, one deeper discussion page rotates every two hours, within the first 1,000 searchable results. Resuming a run keeps its saved page plan. Live rankings can change, so this is not exhaustive coverage.

Native 4.1.1 already restores the direct-call endpoint. Missing paths remain expected input failures. Source 1 · Source 2 · Source 3
  • mysql--bugs--112137: The official report already provides the parallel-reader wait stack, controlled I/O-thread comparisons and a documented synchronous-read repair for MySQL 8.0.37/8.4.0. This report has not established a missing originating caller or task-attribution fact for CoroPerf to recover. No local benchmark or patch was executed. Source 1
  • postgres--mail--da0b1ad82f4faec1b3448678: This specific mail says the async_mode flag placement has no observable effect without timer instrumentation and discusses already-pushed instrumentation changes. It does not establish a reproducible missing-caller problem for CoroPerf. No reproduction was attempted. Source 1 · Source 2
  • apache--flink--flink-41427: The report provides a fully synchronous part-upload call chain and shows that the concurrency setting is never consumed. No missing coroutine caller is established by this report. Read-only review; no S3 workload or patch executed. Source 1

  • ray-project--ray--68086: The report identifies a returned-value classification and callback-contract mismatch: Exception values are mistaken for task failures, and callbacks receive an internal wrapper. No missing-caller evidence is supplied. Ray also documents optional task/actor creation-stack capture, which must be compared before claiming a caller gap. No local Ray workload or patch was executed. Source 1 · Source 2
